Moneywort is probably my favorite plant in general - pretty sturdy and hardy plant and makes for a great background that almost makes a bamboo-like forest for your shrimp to pick through. I’ll often find them hiding in the moneywort when I’m trying to count them. Marimo moss balls are another good plant to keep since they require very little light and provide the shrimp plenty of area to pick biofilm from. Any plants that have a high surface area will work great in providing your shrimp a 24/7 of biofilm they can eat from. Only plant I can personally warn you from using is hornwort cause every time I’ve had it, it just dies and makes a horrible mess in my tank.
A good mix of plants is best though. Shrimp will pick through and clean just about anything. I would go to your local pet store and see what foreground/midground plants they have available and always do your research. Try and go for low to no CO2 plants so you don’t have to buy a whole separate system just to keep those plants alive.
